services.desc: Saturday, September 6 - A botanical garden, by any definition, is a place for things to grow, including trees, plants and flowers, for sure, but also birds, bees, beasties and even some things that go bump in the night. One might call it an eco park. My relationship with the area that now encompasses what is known as the Botanical Garden of the Piedmont occurred before there was a garden, when the land just east of the railroad tracks and the long-established McIntire Park was filled with the leaves collected by the city of Charlottesville during the autumnal raking season as city residents cleared their lawns of fallen leaves.
